knowledge:
- key_parameters: r1=Path to R1 fastq file ;; r2=Path to R2 fastq file ;; restriction=Restriction enzyme(s) used for Hi-C (e.g., 'DpnII,HinfI') ;; binning=Minimum resolution for binning (e.g., 1000) ;; genome=Genome reference (path to .fasta, pre-computed bowtie2 index, or supported ID like 'hg38', 'mm10', 'dm6', 'R64-1-1', 'WBcel235', 'GRCz10', 'Galgal4') ;; output=Directory path where output files will be placed ;; iterative=Logical (default TRUE); if TRUE, performs iterative truncation and alignment to rescue more pairs ;; balancing_args=Character (default " --min-nnz 10 --mad-max 5 "); arguments passed to cooler for matrix normalization ;; threads=Integer (default 1L); number of CPUs to use ;; exclude_chr=Character (default 'Mito|chrM|MT'); chromosomes to remove from the final contact matrix ;; keep_bam=Logical (default FALSE); whether to keep intermediate BAM files ;; scratch=Path to temporary directory for processing (default tempdir())
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Appropriate when processing raw paired-end Hi-C sequencing reads (FASTQ format) into standard, shareable, and normalized contact matrices (.mcool) and interaction pairs (.pairs) within an R environment.
- pitfalls: The first execution of HiCool() will trigger a fresh conda environment installation via basilisk, which may take some time and requires internet access. Iterative mapping (iterative = TRUE) is computationally intensive and takes longer than standard mapping.

workflows.name: hic_processing_pipeline
workflows.intent: Process raw paired-end Hi-C FASTQ files into binned, normalized contact matrices (.mcool) and interaction pairs (.pairs).
workflows.stages: 1. Load the HiCool package ;; 2. Run the HiCool() function with FASTQ inputs, restriction enzymes, binning resolution, genome ID, and output directory ;; 3. Inspect the returned CoolFile object and its metadata
workflows.code:
library(HiCool)
hcf <- HiCool(
    r1 = HiContactsData::HiContactsData(sample = 'yeast_wt', format = 'fastq_R1'), 
    r2 = HiContactsData::HiContactsData(sample = 'yeast_wt', format = 'fastq_R2'), 
    restriction = 'DpnII,HinfI', 
    binning = 1000, 
    genome = 'R64-1-1', 
    output = './HiCool/'
)
hcf
S4Vectors::metadata(hcf)
